note: In-source base theory-capability library. Each record conforms to docs/physics_research_gates/THEORY_CAPABILITY_REQUIREMENT_SPEC (18 gate-callable fields). Merged read-only under the external distilled library's families D/E. Consumed by the Theory gate at the model stage.

capabilities.applicability_question: The task involves a physical model whose variables, DOF, parameters, BC/IC, symmetries and assumptions must be pinned down.
capabilities.non_applicability_condition: The task is a pure literature synthesis or data-only analysis with no model to construct.
capabilities.usage_question: Did Argus actually perform 'Model formalization' for this task (not just mention it)?
capabilities.evidence_question: Which evidence_file shows 'Model formalization' was executed (derivation / notebook / MODEL.md)?
capabilities.minimum_artifact: research/MODEL.md stating variables, parameters, BC/IC and assumptions.
capabilities.recommended_artifacts: MODEL.md + a symbol/parameter table + an explicit statement of what is new vs prior models.
capabilities.basic_standard: Variables, degrees of freedom, parameters, boundary/initial conditions, symmetries and assumptions are stated explicitly.
capabilities.advanced_standard: The model's added terms or restrictions relative to the closest prior model are stated.
capabilities.publishable_standard: The model is stated at a level a reader could reimplement, with every assumption justified.
repair_actions: Perform 'Model formalization' and record evidence_file/evidence_location, or record if_not_used_why.
If a claim depends on it and it was not done, downgrade the claim.
capabilities.claim_downgrade_if_missing: Any claim about the model's behaviour is downgraded to 'model unspecified / inconclusive'.
capabilities.comparison_to_prior_work_requirement: State how the model differs from the closest prior model (added term, changed BC, new regime).
capabilities.example_good_use: Writes MODEL.md with a parameter table, BC/IC, and 'this adds a non-reciprocal hopping term absent in ref [3]'.
capabilities.example_bad_use: Says 'we study an SSH-like model' with no variables, parameters, or assumptions written down.
capabilities.applicability: The task involves a physical model whose variables, DOF, parameters, BC/IC, symmetries and assumptions must be pinned down.
capabilities.basic_criteria: Variables, degrees of freedom, parameters, boundary/initial conditions, symmetries and assumptions are stated explicitly.
capabilities.advanced_criteria: The model's added terms or restrictions relative to the closest prior model are stated.
capabilities.pass_threshold: The model is stated at a level a reader could reimplement, with every assumption justified.

capabilities.applicability_question: The model has tunable couplings, symmetric points, or solvable/continuum limits.
capabilities.non_applicability_condition: The model has no analytic limit and no symmetric/solvable point to exploit.
capabilities.usage_question: Did Argus actually perform 'Limiting-case analysis' for this task (not just mention it)?
capabilities.evidence_question: Which evidence_file shows 'Limiting-case analysis' was executed (derivation / notebook / MODEL.md)?
capabilities.minimum_artifact: A short note listing the relevant limits and expected behaviour in each.
capabilities.recommended_artifacts: Derivations in each limit + a figure/annotation showing the numerics approach the limit.
capabilities.basic_standard: The relevant limits (zero coupling, large/small parameter, symmetric/solvable points) are listed.
capabilities.advanced_standard: A limit result is used to explain the numerics or as a sanity check.
capabilities.publishable_standard: Limit results are derived and quantitatively reconcile with the numerics.
repair_actions: Perform 'Limiting-case analysis' and record evidence_file/evidence_location, or record if_not_used_why.
If a claim depends on it and it was not done, downgrade the claim.
capabilities.claim_downgrade_if_missing: A claim relying on near-limit behaviour is downgraded to 'not analysed near the limit'.
capabilities.comparison_to_prior_work_requirement: State whether prior work analysed the same limits and whether results agree.
capabilities.example_good_use: Checks that at zero non-reciprocity the spectrum matches the known Hermitian result.
capabilities.example_bad_use: Never checks any limit; presents raw numerics with no analytic anchor.
capabilities.applicability: The model has tunable couplings, symmetric points, or solvable/continuum limits.
capabilities.basic_criteria: The relevant limits (zero coupling, large/small parameter, symmetric/solvable points) are listed.
capabilities.advanced_criteria: A limit result is used to explain the numerics or as a sanity check.
capabilities.pass_threshold: Limit results are derived and quantitatively reconcile with the numerics.

capabilities.applicability_question: The model has dimensional parameters and a scaling or control-parameter question.
capabilities.non_applicability_condition: All quantities are already dimensionless and there is no scale to reason about.
capabilities.usage_question: Did Argus actually perform 'Dimensional & scale analysis' for this task (not just mention it)?
capabilities.evidence_question: Which evidence_file shows 'Dimensional & scale analysis' was executed (derivation / notebook / MODEL.md)?
capabilities.minimum_artifact: A parameter/units table + the dimensionless groups.
capabilities.recommended_artifacts: Nondimensionalised equations + a data-collapse figure over the controlling group.
capabilities.basic_standard: Parameters are listed with units and the dimensionless control parameters are identified.
capabilities.advanced_standard: It is explained which parameter combinations control the phenomenon.
capabilities.publishable_standard: A nondimensionalisation makes the controlling group explicit and predicts a collapse.
repair_actions: Perform 'Dimensional & scale analysis' and record evidence_file/evidence_location, or record if_not_used_why.
If a claim depends on it and it was not done, downgrade the claim.
capabilities.claim_downgrade_if_missing: A scaling/universality claim is downgraded to 'control parameter not identified'.
capabilities.comparison_to_prior_work_requirement: State whether prior work identified the same control parameters.
capabilities.example_good_use: Identifies g/J as the single dimensionless knob and shows curves collapse over it.
capabilities.example_bad_use: Reports results vs several raw parameters without identifying the controlling group.
capabilities.applicability: The model has dimensional parameters and a scaling or control-parameter question.
capabilities.basic_criteria: Parameters are listed with units and the dimensionless control parameters are identified.
capabilities.advanced_criteria: It is explained which parameter combinations control the phenomenon.
capabilities.pass_threshold: A nondimensionalisation makes the controlling group explicit and predicts a collapse.

capabilities.applicability_question: The system has symmetries, conservation laws, selection rules, gauge freedom or boundary constraints.
capabilities.non_applicability_condition: The system has no relevant symmetry or constraint bearing on the claims.
capabilities.usage_question: Did Argus actually perform 'Symmetry & constraint analysis' for this task (not just mention it)?
capabilities.evidence_question: Which evidence_file shows 'Symmetry & constraint analysis' was executed (derivation / notebook / MODEL.md)?
capabilities.minimum_artifact: A note stating which symmetries hold and which are broken.
capabilities.recommended_artifacts: Derivation of the symmetry's consequence + numerical confirmation.
capabilities.basic_standard: The relevant symmetries/constraints present or absent are stated.
capabilities.advanced_standard: Their constraints on the spectrum, states, response, or invariants are derived.
capabilities.publishable_standard: A symmetry argument predicts a spectral/degeneracy feature confirmed by the numerics.
repair_actions: Perform 'Symmetry & constraint analysis' and record evidence_file/evidence_location, or record if_not_used_why.
If a claim depends on it and it was not done, downgrade the claim.
capabilities.claim_downgrade_if_missing: A spectral/degeneracy claim is downgraded to 'symmetry not analysed'.
capabilities.comparison_to_prior_work_requirement: State how prior work used the same symmetry and whether the consequence matches.
capabilities.example_good_use: Uses a sublattice symmetry to explain why zero modes come in pairs.
capabilities.example_bad_use: Claims protected modes while ignoring that the relevant symmetry is broken by the terms used.
capabilities.applicability: The system has symmetries, conservation laws, selection rules, gauge freedom or boundary constraints.
capabilities.basic_criteria: The relevant symmetries/constraints present or absent are stated.
capabilities.advanced_criteria: Their constraints on the spectrum, states, response, or invariants are derived.
capabilities.pass_threshold: A symmetry argument predicts a spectral/degeneracy feature confirmed by the numerics.

capabilities.applicability_question: There is a small parameter or a tractable approximation (weak/strong coupling, linearisation, mean field, semiclassical).
capabilities.non_applicability_condition: No small parameter or controlled approximation is available or needed.
capabilities.usage_question: Did Argus actually perform 'Perturbation / approximation control' for this task (not just mention it)?
capabilities.evidence_question: Which evidence_file shows 'Perturbation / approximation control' was executed (derivation / notebook / MODEL.md)?
capabilities.minimum_artifact: A statement of the small parameter and the approximation used.
capabilities.recommended_artifacts: Expansion/derivation + a figure comparing approximation vs numerics with a stated validity range.
capabilities.basic_standard: Whether a controlled small-parameter expansion or approximation applies is identified.
capabilities.advanced_standard: The approximate result is compared against the numerics and its validity range stated.
capabilities.publishable_standard: The approximation's error is bounded and matches the numerics within that bound.
repair_actions: Perform 'Perturbation / approximation control' and record evidence_file/evidence_location, or record if_not_used_why.
If a claim depends on it and it was not done, downgrade the claim.
capabilities.claim_downgrade_if_missing: A claim relying on an approximation is downgraded to 'validity range unchecked'.
capabilities.comparison_to_prior_work_requirement: State whether prior work used the same approximation and in what range.
capabilities.example_good_use: Uses weak-coupling perturbation and shows it tracks the numerics up to g~0.3.
capabilities.example_bad_use: Applies a mean-field result far outside its validity with no check.
capabilities.applicability: There is a small parameter or a tractable approximation (weak/strong coupling, linearisation, mean field, semiclassical).
capabilities.basic_criteria: Whether a controlled small-parameter expansion or approximation applies is identified.
capabilities.advanced_criteria: The approximate result is compared against the numerics and its validity range stated.
capabilities.pass_threshold: The approximation's error is bounded and matches the numerics within that bound.

capabilities.applicability_question: Numerical figures are presented and a mechanism/interpretation is claimed.
capabilities.non_applicability_condition: The work is a pure benchmark/reproduction with no mechanistic claim.
capabilities.usage_question: Did Argus actually perform 'Explanatory power vs description' for this task (not just mention it)?
capabilities.evidence_question: Which evidence_file shows 'Explanatory power vs description' was executed (derivation / notebook / MODEL.md)?
capabilities.minimum_artifact: A short explanation paragraph per main figure.
capabilities.recommended_artifacts: A mechanism section that derives the observed feature and predicts a new one.
capabilities.basic_standard: Every main numerical phenomenon has a theory explanation paragraph, not just a caption.
capabilities.advanced_standard: The theory predicts a result not yet computed.
capabilities.publishable_standard: The theoretical account is quantitative and predicts a new, then-confirmed result.
repair_actions: Perform 'Explanatory power vs description' and record evidence_file/evidence_location, or record if_not_used_why.
If a claim depends on it and it was not done, downgrade the claim.
capabilities.claim_downgrade_if_missing: A mechanism claim without theory is downgraded to 'observed, mechanism unexplained'.
capabilities.comparison_to_prior_work_requirement: State how the explanation compares to prior theoretical accounts of the same phenomenon.
capabilities.example_good_use: Explains the skin accumulation via spectral winding and predicts its size dependence.
capabilities.example_bad_use: Describes the figures in words and calls the description a 'mechanism'.
capabilities.applicability: Numerical figures are presented and a mechanism/interpretation is claimed.
capabilities.basic_criteria: Every main numerical phenomenon has a theory explanation paragraph, not just a caption.
capabilities.advanced_criteria: The theory predicts a result not yet computed.
capabilities.pass_threshold: The theoretical account is quantitative and predicts a new, then-confirmed result.
